title: Load Balancer Overview
description: Understand how Azure Load Balancer distributes traffic across healthy VMs or services.

data.text: What Does a Load Balancer Do?

Azure Load Balancer is a layer-4 (TCP/UDP) load balancer. It distributes incoming traffic across healthy virtual machines or cloud services. If one instance goes down, the load balancer stops sending traffic to it.
Load Balancer comes in two SKUs: Basic (for testing) and Standard (for production). Standard supports availability zones, multiple frontends, and outbound rules.

data.title: Load Balancer Concepts
items: Frontend IP — the IP address clients connect to
Backend pool — the VMs or scale sets receiving traffic
Health probes — checks that determine if an instance is healthy
Load balancing rules — map frontend ports to backend ports
Inbound NAT rules — map a specific port to a specific VM for management

data.title: Create a Standard Load Balancer
data.content: Provision a load balancer with a health probe and a load balancing rule.
data.code:
# Create the load balancer
az network lb create   --name myLoadBalancer   --resource-group myRG   --sku Standard   --frontend-ip-name lb-frontend   --backend-pool-name lb-backend

# Create a health probe on port 80
az network lb probe create   --lb-name myLoadBalancer   --resource-group myRG   --name http-probe   --protocol Http   --port 80   --path "/health"

# Create a load balancing rule
az network lb rule create   --lb-name myLoadBalancer   --resource-group myRG   --name http-rule   --probe-name http-probe   --protocol Tcp   --frontend-port 80   --backend-port 80   --frontend-ip-name lb-frontend   --backend-pool-name lb-backend

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Load Balancer is a layer-4 TCP/UDP distributor.
Health probes detect unhealthy instances automatically.
Use Standard SKU for production; Basic SKU has no SLA.
data.takeaway: Use Load Balancer when you need simple TCP/UDP distribution across identical instances.
